official.deadline_note: Earlier gates apply: October 2, 2026 deadline to submit the eligibility verification form (which opens the application), and October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET deadline for referees to submit all three reference letters. Applications open September 1, 2026. Two mandatory information sessions are held in the weeks of October 5 and October 12, 2026.
official.status_note: The application process for the 2027 Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship is open, from September 1 to November 6, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. (ET), via the two-step process (eligibility screening, then full application).
official.tuition_coverage_note: An annual stipend of up to $50,000 for three years to cover tuition and living expenses related to doctoral studies; an additional annual allowance of up to $20,000 per year for three years supports research, networking, and travel related to the doctoral project and Foundation programming.
official.funding_period: per year (up to, for three years)
benefits: Annual stipend of up to $50,000 for three years to cover tuition and living expenses related to doctoral studies
Annual allowance of up to $20,000 for three years to support research, networking activities, and travel related to the doctoral project and Foundation programming
Membership in the Foundation's community of Scholars, Fellows and Mentors
Lifelong membership in the Foundation's alumni network of more than 500 individuals
Mentorship and experiential learning: meetings, masterclasses, seminars and field experiences designed to broaden perspectives and connect Scholars with Mentors, Fellows and Scholars
Disbursed in three instalments per year; Scholars may work part-time up to 20 hours per week while receiving full benefits
eligibility: At the time of application the applicant must be in the first year or the second year of a PhD program
The field of study must be broadly related to the humanities or social sciences and address issues relevant to Canada's future
The PhD research must align with at least one of the Foundation's four themes: Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment

The applicant must be one of the following: a Canadian student enrolled at a Canadian university; a Canadian student enrolled at a university outside Canada; or an international student enrolled at a Canadian university
International students residing outside Canada or enrolled at a university outside Canada are not eligible
Applicants must demonstrate outstanding academic achievement and a high level of intellectual ability, assessed across the whole application including transcripts and letters of recommendation
There is no age limit to apply
There is no requirement to be fluent in both official languages; applicants must be able to communicate effectively in either French or English
requirements: Complete the short eligibility screening form on the SmartSimple portal (https://fdnpetf.smartsimple.ca) by October 2, 2026; only applicants whose eligibility is confirmed gain access to the full application form
Applications that do not meet the eligibility criteria will not be reviewed; only applications that meet the program's eligibility criteria will be assessed
Provide exactly three letters of reference - one from the PhD supervisor, one from another academic referee, and one from a referee outside academia - no more and no fewer
Reference letters must be attached within the application file; they cannot be sent directly to the Foundation, and you cannot submit your application if the reference letters are not attached

If the PhD supervisor has not yet been chosen or does not know the applicant well, a former supervisor or another professor may act as referee, with an explanation in the Special Circumstances section of the application
The application form must be filled out in one language only, either English or French
Attend a mandatory information session offered in the week of October 5 or October 12, 2026
documents: Completed eligibility screening form (available from September 1, 2026 on the SmartSimple portal https://fdnpetf.smartsimple.ca)
Completed full application form (SmartSimple portal), including the research proposal and the Special Circumstances section where relevant
Three letters of reference: one from the PhD supervisor, one from another academic referee, and one from a referee outside academia, attached within the application file
Release/authorization and required documentation for the funding agreement once selected, as stated in the application form
Contact information for any Indigenous status identification if applicable (per Foundation practice)
selection_criteria: Academic excellence, supported by an outstanding academic record
The clear alignment of the research project with the Foundation's mission and four founding themes
The rigour of the research proposal
The ability to share knowledge for the benefit of society
Exceptional potential to advance knowledge and address the major challenges facing Canada and the world
Willingness to engage in dialogue, interdisciplinary collaboration, and knowledge sharing
coverage: Annual stipend of up to $50,000 for three years to cover tuition and living expenses related to doctoral studies
Annual allowance of up to $20,000 for three years to support research, networking activities, and travel related to the doctoral work

For Scholars studying outside Canada receiving external funding in foreign currency, the Foundation converts that amount into Canadian dollars; the location of study does not affect the Scholarship amount

Regardless of other funding, all Scholars receive the full annual $20,000 allowance and a minimum of $25,000 from the annual stipend; the value of the Scholarship is adjusted based on amounts received from other organizations, institutions or universities, and all additional sources of income must be declared annually
application_method: Review the published eligibility criteria to confirm the profile meets all requirements.
Complete the short eligibility screening form on the SmartSimple portal (https://fdnpetf.smartsimple.ca) by October 2, 2026.
Wait for the Foundation to confirm eligibility and grant access to the full application form.
Attend a mandatory information session in the week of October 5 or October 12, 2026.
Complete the full application form in English or French (one language only), including the research proposal and the Special Circumstances section where relevant.

Nominate exactly three referees within the application file so they receive access to the letter instructions; referees must submit their letters by October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET, and letters must be attached within the application file.
Submit the complete application by November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET.
Applicants receive a confirmation email acknowledging submission; the application form is removed from the portal once the competition ends.
official.application_route: Self-applied, two-step online process on the Foundation's SmartSimple portal: first submit the eligibility screening form (deadline October 2, 2026) to unlock access to the full application, then complete and submit the full application by November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET.
official.study_mode: Full-time doctoral study at time of application and during the Scholarship (payments pause and the Scholarship may be suspended up to one year if the Scholar must take leave; part-time work up to 20 hours per week is permitted alongside full benefits)
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be a Canadian student enrolled at a Canadian university, a Canadian student enrolled at a university outside Canada, or an international student enrolled at a Canadian university; international students residing outside Canada or enrolled at a university outside Canada are not eligible.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - international (non-Canadian) students are eligible only if enrolled in a doctoral program at a Canadian university; Canadian students may pursue their doctoral studies either in Canada or abroad.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Doctoral field broadly related to the humanities or social sciences and addressing issues relevant to Canada's future; PhD research must align with at least one of the Foundation's four founding themes: Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment.
official.research_requirement: Yes - the application includes a research proposal, and applications are assessed in part on the rigour of the research proposal and its alignment with the Foundation's mission and four founding themes.
official.description: The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation PhD scholarship supports doctoral students with an excellent academic record who are engaged in humanities and social sciences research that contributes to the advancement of Canada and society. As a Scholar you receive an annual stipend of up to $50,000 and an annual research and travel allowance of up to $20,000 for three years, plus membership in the Foundation's community of Scholars, Fellows and Mentors, mentorship and experiential learning, and a network of more than 500 alumni.
official.english_requirement: Applicants must be able to communicate effectively in either French or English; fluency in both official languages is not required. The application form may be completed in English or French, in one language only, and referees may respond in either language regardless of the language of the application. No IELTS or TOEFL score is published as a requirement on the official pages reviewed.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a $50,000-per-year stipend plus a separate $20,000-per-year research, travel and networking allowance for three years, so plan your budget around up to $70,000 per year of Foundation support, with the scholarship value reduced by any other scholarships you hold but never below $25,000 of stipend per year. Your application path is strictly sequential: the eligibility form gates the full application, the references gate submission, and the final application gate is November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET. Because you must be in year one or two of your PhD at the time you apply with humanities/social-sciences research tied to one of the Foundation's four themes, treat eligibility screening in September as your single biggest funnel risk. Build your proposal to show knowledge mobilization and community impact explicitly, since the Foundation ranks the ability to share knowledge for the benefit of society on par with conventional academic measures.
applicant_utility.best_fit: First- or second-year humanities and social sciences PhD students - Canadian students anywhere in the world, or international students enrolled at a Canadian university - with strong transcripts, a research project aligned to one of the Foundation's four themes, and a record of civic or community engagement they can evidence.
application_readiness_checklist: Diarize all four dates as hard gates: September 1, 2026 (form opens), October 2, 2026 (eligibility form), October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET (all three references received), November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET (full application)

Line up your three referees - supervisor, second academic, and one outside academia (not a family member) - and confirm they can upload directly inside the application file before the October 30 cutoff
Map your research explicitly onto at least one of the four founding themes in the proposal itself, not just in the cover letter, and name the Canadian relevance
If your supervisor is new to you or not yet confirmed, draft the Special Circumstances explanation early rather than leaving it to referees
Register for and attend one of the mandatory information sessions in the weeks of October 5 or October 12, 2026
Decide now whether you apply in English or French - the whole form must be in one language, though referees may answer in either
Prepare a budget showing how the up-to-$50,000 stipend covers tuition and living costs and how the up-to-$20,000 allowance funds research, networking and travel, since both are annual for three years
Plan to keep a copy of your application, because the portal removes the form once the competition closes and the confirmation email is your only proof of submission
common_rejection_risks: Missing the October 2, 2026 eligibility-form deadline, which is the real cut-off point since it blocks all later steps
Being in year three or beyond of the PhD at the time of application, which makes you ineligible regardless of record
A research topic that is only implicitly related to one of the four themes, so alignment with the Foundation's mission reads as weak
Submitting more or fewer than exactly three references, or having letters sent outside the application file instead of uploaded within it
Choosing a non-academic referee who cannot speak to real commitments beyond campus, or who is a family member (expressly not permitted)
Writing an application in mixed English and French, which is not allowed
Treating the stipend as guaranteed: the amount is 'up to' $50,000 and is adjusted down by other awards declared annually
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The Foundation's pages describe coverage of tuition and living expenses (up to $50,000 per year) and research, networking and travel (up to $20,000 per year), but publish no itemised cap list; applicants must assume any tuition or living costs beyond the awarded 'up to' values, income-tax treatment of the stipend and allowance, and any family or relocation costs are their own responsibility.
document_audit: The three references must live inside your application file - letters sent to the Foundation separately will not be accepted and an application with missing letters cannot be submitted at all
Exactly three referees are allowed; extra letters cannot be added and absent letters cannot be waived
If your supervisor relationship is not typical, the Special Circumstances section is the only sanctioned place to explain it - referees should not be asked to justify it in their letters
The application form must be completed in one language only, so draft in a single language from the start to avoid retranslation work
Once the competition ends the form disappears from the portal, so keep your own complete copy of every submitted component
alerts: The October 2, 2026 eligibility deadline sits a month before the final deadline - treat that as the true application deadline in your own planning
References are due October 30 at 9:00 a.m. ET, one week before the final deadline, so referees must be nominated inside the portal in advance
The stipend is 'up to' $50,000 and is reduced by other funding you hold, with all other income declared annually; there is no guarantee of the full figure
Attending a mandatory information session is part of the process, and skipping it puts your application at risk
International students must be enrolled at a Canadian university - if you are applying from abroad as a non-Canadian, you are not eligible
Funds start only after Board of Directors approval, signature of the funding agreement and submission of required documentation, so your first instalment will arrive after award, not at application
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Self-applied online through the Foundation's SmartSimple portal (https://fdnpetf.smartsimple.ca): submit the short eligibility screening form by October 2, 2026, wait to be granted access to the full application, upload your form and three attached reference letters, and submit the complete application by November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET, receiving a confirmation email as your only proof of submission.
